channel.title: Nicotine Science and Policy
channel.description: Daily digest of views, debates and discussions on nicotine science, policy, regulation and advocacy.

item.title: Sweden leads EU rebellion against Poland’s tough vape and nicotine curbs, as smoking death toll hits 56,000 a year
item.description: Sweden’s challenge to Poland’s tough vape and nicotine restrictions is more than a procedural dispute. It raises a fundamental question for Europe: should countries with some of the best smoking outcomes be ignored when they point to the role of safer nicotine products? With tens of thousands of smoking-related deaths still recorded each year, policy should be guided by evidence of what reduces harm, not by reflexive restrictions on every new product. Europe should learn from success before legislating against it. (Published on August 06, 2026bysmokefreesweden.org)

item.title: One Letter. One Question. Thousands of Kilometres.
item.description: One letter can expose a much larger failure. When thousands of people who smoke are reduced to policy abstractions, the most important question is often left unanswered: what options are they actually being given? Tobacco harm reduction is not only about products or regulation; it is about whether public health listens to the people most affected by its decisions. A system that speaks for smokers without hearing them is unlikely to help them move away from harm. (Published on August 06, 2026bysubstack.com)

item.title: Is Prohibition Making Things Worse? | GFN Voices 2026 #2
item.description: Prohibition often promises fewer problems, but the aftermath tells a different story. Once safer nicotine products are pushed out of legal reach, people do not simply stop wanting them — they find other routes, often with less oversight and more risk. For smokers, that can mean returning to cigarettes or relying on unregulated supply. The real test is not whether prohibition sounds protective, but whether it leaves people safer than before. (Published on August 06, 2026bygfn.tv)

item.title: Experts Recommend Physicians Use Vape to Help Smokers Quit
item.description: Doctors are often the first trusted voice a smoker hears when trying to quit. If evidence supports vaping as a cessation aid, clinicians should be able to discuss it honestly rather than avoid the subject because of stigma. The goal is not to promote nicotine use, but to help people move away from combustible tobacco when other methods have not worked. Smoking cessation advice should reflect the full range of evidence-based options available to adults. (Published on August 06, 2026bytobaccoreporter.com)
